title: RHom base change for a perfect complex
statement: Let A\to A' be a morphism of commutative rings. Regard complexes of A-modules (resp. A'-modules) as complexes of modules over the ringed site with one object and ring A (resp. A'), so that RHom_A, RHom_{A'} denote the derived Hom of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] for these ringed sites and A'\otimes_A^L- the derived change of rings of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], computed by K-flat resolutions. Let E be a perfect complex of A-modules, i.e. E is isomorphic in D(A) to a bounded complex of finite projective A-modules (equivalently \widetilde E is perfect on Spec(A) in the sense of [def-pc-perfect-complex], by [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective]), and let K be any complex of A-modules. The canonical map A'\otimes_A^L RHom_A(E,K)\to RHom_{A'}(A'\otimes_A^L E,A'\otimes_A^L K), namely the A'-linear extension of the A-linear map RHom_A(E,K)\to RHom_{A'}(A'\otimes_A^L E,A'\otimes_A^L K) induced by the functor A'\otimes_A^L-, is an isomorphism in D(A').

source.place: RHom base-change lemma for a perfect complex, clause (1)

proof.text: Choose a bounded complex P^\bullet of finite projective A-modules representing E (the definition in the statement). Choose a K-flat resolution Q^\bullet\to K [lem-pc-kflat-resolution, def-pc-kflat-complex], and the K-injective resolution Q^\bullet\to I^\bullet used in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. A bounded complex is bounded above and its terms are projective, so [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective] makes P^\bullet K-projective; applying Hom_A^\bullet(P^\bullet,-) to the acyclic cone of Q^\bullet\to I^\bullet shows that Hom_A^\bullet(P^\bullet,Q^\bullet)\to Hom_A^\bullet(P^\bullet,I^\bullet) is a quasi-isomorphism, so Hom_A^\bullet(P^\bullet,Q^\bullet) represents RHom_A(E,K) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

source.place: Lemma 0A6A (label lemma-base-change-RHom), map (equation-base-change-RHom), clause (1), bounded finite-projective model

proof.text: For a bounded finite-projective P^\bullet, each degree of Hom_A^\bullet(P^\bullet,Q^\bullet) is a finite product of terms Hom_A(P^i,Q^{i+n}). For every finite projective P^i, scalar extension gives the canonical isomorphism A'\otimes_A Hom_A(P^i,Q^{i+n}) \cong Hom_{A'}(A'\otimes_A P^i,A'\otimes_A Q^{i+n}); these degreewise isomorphisms commute with the differentials because they are induced by the same evaluation maps. Thus tensoring the Hom complex with A' identifies it with the Hom complex of A'\otimes_A P^\bullet and A'\otimes_A Q^\bullet. This is the finite-projective tensor-Hom calculation, including the zero and finite-free summand cases, written directly from the definitions.

source.place: Lemma 0A6A (label lemma-base-change-RHom), map (equation-base-change-RHom), clause (1), finite-projective tensor-Hom calculation

proof.text: Hom_A^\bullet(P^\bullet,Q^\bullet) is K-flat, so A'\otimes_A Hom_A^\bullet(P^\bullet,Q^\bullet) represents A'\otimes_A^L RHom_A(E,K) [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Indeed, for finite projective P^i the natural map Hom_A(P^i,A)\otimes_A M\to Hom_A(P^i,M) is an isomorphism (true for A^n, hence for summands), so Hom_A^\bullet(P^\bullet,Q^\bullet)\cong Tot(P^\vee\otimes_A Q^\bullet) with P^\vee=Hom_A^\bullet(P^\bullet,A) a bounded complex of finite projective, hence flat, A-modules. For an acyclic F^\bullet, Tot(F^\bullet\otimes Tot(P^\vee\otimes Q^\bullet))\cong Tot(Tot(F^\bullet\otimes P^\vee)\otimes Q^\bullet); Tot(F^\bullet\otimes P^\vee) is acyclic by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], hence so is the whole since Q^\bullet is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex].

source.place: Lemma 0A6A (label lemma-base-change-RHom), map (equation-base-change-RHom), clause (1), K-flatness of the Hom complex

proof.text: By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], A'\otimes_A Q^\bullet represents A'\otimes_A^L K and A'\otimes_A P^\bullet (bounded, flat terms, K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]) represents A'\otimes_A^L E. Each A'\otimes_A P^i is finite projective over A' (a direct summand of a finite free module after scalar extension), so by [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective] and the argument of Step 1 over A', Hom_{A'}^\bullet(A'\otimes_A P^\bullet,A'\otimes_A Q^\bullet) represents RHom_{A'}(A'\otimes_A^L E,A'\otimes_A^L K) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. On these representatives the map induced by the functor A'\otimes_A^L- (computed on the K-flat complexes P^\bullet, Q^\bullet by the termwise functor A'\otimes_A-) is \varphi\mapsto 1\otimes\varphi, Hom_A^\bullet(P^\bullet,Q^\bullet)\to Hom_{A'}^\bullet(A'\otimes_AP^\bullet,A'\otimes_AQ^\bullet), and its A'-linear extension, on the representative of Step 3, is the chain map a'\otimes\varphi\mapsto a'(1\otimes\varphi), which is the isomorphism of Step 2. Hence the canonical map is an isomorphism.
